questions.stem: A particle executes simple harmonic motion with an amplitude $A$. At what distance from the mean position is its kinetic energy equal to its potential energy?
questions.solution:
Kinetic energy $K = \frac{1}{2} m \omega^2 (A^2 - x^2)$.
Potential energy $U = \frac{1}{2} m \omega^2 x^2$.
Given $K = U \implies A^2 - x^2 = x^2 \implies 2x^2 = A^2 \implies x = \frac{A}{\sqrt{2}}$.

questions.stem: The equation of motion of a particle executing simple harmonic motion is given by $x = 10 \sin\left(10\pi t + \frac{\pi}{3}\right)\ \mathrm{m}$. The time period of the motion is $T = \frac{1}{x}\ \mathrm{s}$. The value of $x$ is _________.
questions.solution:
Comparing the given equation with $x = A \sin(\omega t + \phi)$, we get $\omega = 10\pi\ \mathrm{rad/s}$.
Since $T = \frac{2\pi}{\omega} = \frac{2\pi}{10\pi} = \frac{1}{5}\ \mathrm{s}$.
Comparing with $T = \frac{1}{x}$, we find $x = 5$.

questions.stem: The equation of a simple harmonic motion is given by $x = 5 \sin\left(2\pi t + \frac{\pi}{4}\right)\ \mathrm{m}$. The state of motion of the particle at $t = 1\ \mathrm{s}$ is given by:

options.label: A
options.content: Position $= \frac{5}{\sqrt{2}}\ \mathrm{m}$, direction of motion is positive

options.label: B
options.content: Position $= \frac{5}{\sqrt{2}}\ \mathrm{m}$, direction of motion is negative

options.label: C
options.content: Position $= -\frac{5}{\sqrt{2}}\ \mathrm{m}$, direction of motion is positive

options.label: D
options.content: Position $= -\frac{5}{\sqrt{2}}\ \mathrm{m}$, direction of motion is negative

questions.solution:
At $t = 1\ \mathrm{s}$, $x = 5 \sin(2\pi + \pi/4) = 5 \sin(\pi/4) = \frac{5}{\sqrt{2}}\ \mathrm{m}$.
Velocity $v = \frac{dx}{dt} = 10\pi \cos\left(2\pi t + \frac{\pi}{4}\right)$.
At $t=1\ \mathrm{s}$, $v = 10\pi \cos(2\pi + \pi/4) = 10\pi \cos(\pi/4) > 0$. So, direction is positive.

questions.stem: An expression for the displacement of a particle executing simple harmonic motion is given by $y = 3 \sin \omega t + 4 \cos \omega t\ \mathrm{m}$. The maximum speed of the particle is $10\ \mathrm{m/s}$. The time period of the motion is $\frac{\pi}{x}\ \mathrm{s}$. The value of $x$ is ______.
questions.solution:
The given SHM equation can be written as $y = A \sin(\omega t + \phi)$,
where $A = \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = 5\ \mathrm{m}$.
The maximum speed is $v_{\text{max}} = A\omega = 10\ \mathrm{m/s}$.
Thus, $5\omega = 10 \implies \omega = 2\ \mathrm{rad/s}$.
The time period is $T = \frac{2\pi}{\omega} = \frac{2\pi}{2} = \pi\ \mathrm{s}$.
Comparing with $T = \frac{\pi}{x}$, we get $x = 1$.

questions.stem: A particle executes simple harmonic motion with an amplitude $A$. The ratio of its kinetic energy to its potential energy when it is at a distance of $\frac{A}{2}$ from the mean position is:
questions.solution:
Kinetic energy: $K = \frac{1}{2}m\omega^2(A^2 - x^2)$.
Potential energy: $U = \frac{1}{2}m\omega^2 x^2$.
At $x = \frac{A}{2}$:
$K = \frac{1}{2}m\omega^2\left(A^2 - \frac{A^2}{4}\right) = \frac{3}{4}\left(\frac{1}{2}m\omega^2 A^2\right)$.
$U = \frac{1}{2}m\omega^2\left(\frac{A^2}{4}\right) = \frac{1}{4}\left(\frac{1}{2}m\omega^2 A^2\right)$.
Ratio $\frac{K}{U} = \frac{3/4}{1/4} = 3 : 1$.
